propositions: Outbound mapper's assignee resolver is injected as an undeclared attribute rather than passed as a constructor or method parameter, making the dependency invisible to type checkers and discoverable only via getattr with silent fallback.

Attribute injection conceals resolver absence: if injection fails, all assignee resolution silently degrades to non-authoritative results, causing infinite re-emission of assignee changes (ace2 churn class).
Data Center adapter's resolver getattr sits in dead code when attribute is never set, because the injection site and consumption site are decoupled and the contract is not enforced.
Resolver must be threaded explicitly through OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee port signature, both Cloud and DC implementers, and the intermediate diff_canonical_fields call.
DC's constructor-bound resolver and core's per-issue resolver have different lifecycles; explicit parameter with fallback preserves current overwrite semantics where core wins.
